subject: social
title: NC and USA Symbols
about: North Carolina's state symbols (cardinal, dogwood, pine, the N and C flag, Tar Heel State, gray squirrel and more) and the main United States symbols (50 stars, 13 stripes, bald eagle, Washington D.C.). Not named in any NC K-2 objective; tagged to 1.B.1.1 as local traditions and enrichment most NC first-grade classes include.
tip: Spot a cardinal, a pine or a dogwood outside and ask what it is the state symbol of.

cards.q: What is North Carolina's state bird?
cards.note: The male cardinal is bright red. Cardinals stay in North Carolina all year.

cards.q: What is North Carolina's state flower?
cards.note: The dogwood tree blooms in spring with white or pink flowers.

cards.q: What is North Carolina's state tree?
cards.note: Pine trees stay green all year long.

cards.q: Which two big gold letters are on the North Carolina flag?
cards.note: N and C stand for North Carolina. The gold letters sit on each side of a white star on the blue part of the flag.

cards.q: What are North Carolina's two state colors?
cards.note: You can see both state colors on the North Carolina flag.

cards.q: What is North Carolina's nickname?
cards.note: People from North Carolina are called Tar Heels. North Carolina is also called the Old North State.

cards.q: What is North Carolina's state mammal?
cards.note: A mammal is an animal with fur or hair. Gray squirrels live in parks and yards all over North Carolina.

cards.q: What is North Carolina's state insect?
cards.note: Honeybees make honey and help flowers and crops grow.

cards.q: What is North Carolina's state reptile?
cards.note: A reptile has scales. The eastern box turtle can close its shell up tight like a box.

cards.q: What is North Carolina's state dog?
cards.note: The Plott Hound was first raised in the mountains of North Carolina.

cards.q: What is North Carolina's state vegetable?
cards.note: North Carolina grows more sweet potatoes than any other state.

cards.q: What is North Carolina's state drink?
cards.note: Milk helps build strong bones and teeth.

cards.q: What is North Carolina's state red berry?
cards.note: Strawberries are picked in North Carolina in the spring.

cards.q: North Carolina has two state berries. One is the strawberry. What is the other one?
cards.note: Blueberries are picked in North Carolina in the summer.

cards.q: How many stars are on the United States flag?
cards.note: There is one star for each of the 50 states.

cards.q: How many stripes are on the United States flag?
cards.note: There is one stripe for each of the first 13 states.

cards.q: What colors are on the United States flag?
cards.note: The stripes are red and white. The stars are white on the blue part in the corner.

cards.q: What is the national bird of the United States?
cards.note: A bald eagle is not really bald. It has white feathers on its head.

cards.q: What is the capital of the United States?
cards.note: Raleigh is the capital of North Carolina. Washington, D.C. is the capital of the whole country.

cards.q: What is the big green statue holding a torch in New York Harbor?
cards.note: The Statue of Liberty was a gift to the United States from France.
